meta.title: Accessibility statement — Refugio Sensorial
meta.description: Refugio Sensorial's WCAG 2.2 AA conformance statement. Commitments, evaluated criteria, and contact channels to report accessibility issues.

accesibilidad.heading: Accessibility statement
accesibilidad.intro: Refugio Sensorial is designed by and for neurodivergent people. We are committed to meeting WCAG 2.2 level AA guidelines and continuously improving the experience for all users, regardless of their abilities or assistive technologies.
accesibilidad.scoreSummary: {{pass}} of {{total}} evaluated criteria meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
commitments: Full keyboard navigation on every page
"Skip to main content" link visible on focus
Alt text on every non-text element
Text-to-speech (TTS) available on resources and crisis signals
ARIA roles and live regions for dynamic announcements
Visible focus indicators on every interactive element
Correct HTML semantics with landmarks, headings, and lists
Forms with labels, error messages, and aria-invalid
limitations: The interactive Leaflet map has limited keyboard support for individual markers. Map data is also available in text form.
Some color-contrast values on dynamic elements (category badges) may fall below 4.5:1 in edge cases. We're reviewing the palette.
The 3D visuals (logo and background) are decorative and don't affect content; they only render if the device supports WebGL.
accesibilidad.contactText: If you run into an accessibility barrier or something that doesn't work well with your assistive technology, let us know. Your feedback is essential to improving.

meltdown: Talking a lot or giving complex instructions
Touching the person without their explicit permission
Asking them to calm down or stop (they can't)
Trying to reason or explain during the crisis
Publicly drawing attention to what's happening
shutdown: Forcing eye contact or a verbal response
Reading the silence as anger or rejection
Bombarding them with questions or decisions
Turning on bright lights or raising the volume
Demanding they "snap out of it" with no recovery time
burnout: Comparing to how they used to be or how much they could do
Suggesting they "just need to go out more" or socialize
Ignoring the signs of exhaustion and hoping it passes on its own
Pushing to resume normal routines too soon

duracion.meltdown: Minutes to hours. The nervous system needs time to de-escalate and return to baseline.
duracion.shutdown: Hours to days. Recovery is gradual — forcing the pace only makes it longer.
duracion.burnout: Weeks or months. Burnout requires a sustained reduction in load, not just one day of rest.
